report.scene_summary: The video shows a warehouse environment with high-bay racking, open aisles, and staged goods. Pedestrians and material handling equipment (forklifts) are present. The scene is well-lit, but visual obstructions caused by stacked goods and racking structures create potential blind spots where pedestrians and vehicles may not see each other.

findings.title: Pedestrian-Vehicle Blind Spot at Aisle End
findings.location: Zone Z03, specifically the intersection of the main aisle and the cross-aisle on the left side.
findings.observation: A pedestrian in a white suit is observed standing or walking near the end of a rack row in Zone Z03 (E016, E017). A forklift is visible further down the main aisle. The rack structure and stacked boxes at the end of the aisle create a blind corner. A pedestrian entering the main aisle from this cross-aisle, or a forklift turning into this aisle, would not have a clear view of the other until they are very close.
findings.risk_interpretation: This is a classic blind corner scenario. A pedestrian stepping out from behind the rack or a forklift turning the corner could collide with the other party who cannot see them in time to stop. This relates to the requirement for a clear view of the path of travel.
findings.applicability_reason: The obstruction (racks/boxes) hides pedestrians and vehicles from each other at a travel path intersection.
recommended_actions: Install a convex mirror at the aisle end to provide a view of the intersecting path.
Mark a stop line for vehicles and pedestrians at the intersection.
Implement a 'horn at blind corners' policy.
Consider physical separation (guardrails) if traffic volume is high.

findings.title: Obstructed View of Path of Travel by Staged Goods
findings.location: Zone Z02 and Z06, the area with stacked pallets of boxes on the right side of the main aisle.
findings.observation: Multiple pallets of boxes are staged in Zone Z02/Z06, enclosed by yellow floor markings. A pedestrian is seen standing near these stacks (E014, E022). A forklift is also present in this zone (E026, E027). The height of the stacked boxes can obstruct the view of a forklift driver looking forward or to the side, and can hide a pedestrian from the forklift driver's view.
findings.risk_interpretation: If a forklift is moving through this zone with a load, its forward view may be blocked by the boxes. Even without a load, the stacked goods create a visual barrier between the forklift and pedestrians in or near the zone.
findings.applicability_reason: Stacked goods obstruct the driver's view of the path of travel and potential pedestrians.
unknowns: Pedestrian movement patterns within the zone
recommended_actions: Ensure stacked goods do not exceed a safe height that obstructs the driver's view.
If loads obstruct view, require travel with the load trailing.
Mark pedestrian walkways clearly around the staging area.
Use spotters if visibility is consistently poor.

findings.title: Pedestrian Walking Near Vehicle Path
findings.location: Zone Z01 and Z02, along the main aisle and near the staged goods.
findings.observation: Pedestrians are observed walking in the main aisle (Z01) and near the staged goods (Z02). For example, a pedestrian in a yellow vest walks along the yellow line in Z02 (E015, E035). Another pedestrian in white walks in the main aisle (E012, E013). While they are near marked lines, they are in close proximity to where forklifts would travel.
findings.risk_interpretation: Pedestrians sharing the same space as vehicles without physical separation are at risk of collision. The marked lines may not be sufficient to prevent accidental encroachment.
findings.applicability_reason: Aisles and passageways must be kept clear and appropriately marked to separate pedestrian and vehicle traffic.
recommended_actions: Enforce strict separation of pedestrian and vehicle traffic where possible.
Ensure pedestrian walkways are clearly marked and unobstructed.
Train pedestrians to stay within marked zones.
Train forklift operators to be aware of pedestrians and yield when necessary.
